AUTO MODE: the autoMode block below is a deliberately REPO-NEUTRAL profile (decided 2026-10-07): it inherits the built-in entries via "$defaults" and adds only facts true in every repo on this machine. It must never name a specific repo, path, or private data location, because this file is PUBLIC (~/.claude is a symlink to this repo's .claude/) and because autoMode.environment is ONE global value that every repo inherits. Claude Code reads autoMode only from user, --settings flag, and managed settings, and ignores it in any repo's .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json, so a per-repo profile has no home. /auto-mode-setup always writes here, whatever scope it offers, so each run overwrites this block with a profile of the repo it ran in. If that happens, restore this block and the model pin from git; do not move the generated profile into the repo it describes, where it would be inert. settings.local.json in this directory is read only as the project-local file for sessions rooted in this repo, not as a user-level overlay. See docs/assessments/config-propagation.md. ATTRIBUTION: attribution.sessionUrl is false on purpose. It suppresses the Claude-Session trailer that web and Remote Control sessions otherwise append to commits and PR bodies, and it flips the instruction the CLI injects into each session to its do-not-attribute variant, so the harness and CLAUDE.md agree instead of contradicting each other. A gitAttribution key sat here from 2026-02-17 looking like it did this job and was inert: no trace of it in CLI 2.1.250 through 2.1.258 or in the changelog back to 0.2.21. Do not re-add it. environment: ### Scott's machine (applies in every repo, repo-neutral on purpose)

**Trusted repo**: whichever git repository the session's working directory is in, plus its origin remote. Directly mutating a different repo than the working one is out of scope unless the user asks for it in this session.

**Secrets management**: 1Password CLI (`op`), TouchID-gated, with `--account` passed explicitly. No plaintext secrets at rest: resolving a secret into a file, `.env`, or config is a violation unless that repo's own CLAUDE.md names a `.env` convention. Headless runs receive secrets as environment variables, never in argv.

**Public repos**: several repos on this machine are public on GitHub, and ~/.claude is itself a symlink into one (scottwb/dotfiles). Writing private material (client names, another repo's paths or contents, credentials) into a tracked file under ~/.claude is data exfiltration.
**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment.
